properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: hash.js@1.1.3 (SHA-1/SHA-2 hash implementations) ships in the build as a transitive dependency of the Ethereum JS toolchain (ethereumjs-util → create-hash → hash.js). No direct call site in this repo's own scripts, but it is part of what the build installs and is reachable through ethereumjs-util's hashing helpers.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Test/deployment harness compares keccak256 digests of on-chain runtime bytecode, retrieved via a MockCodeCheck contract, against expected constants with `!==` to decide whether each immutable-create2 factory still needs deploying. Compared values are public code hashes — no secret, no attacker-controlled MAC input — so the timing side-channel the rule targets is not exploitable in a local deployment harness. Recorded as the lowest-severity posture pattern.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Ed25519 capability resolved into the install tree via tweetnacl@0.14.5 (yarn.lock:7173), transitive dependency of the truffle/ganache-cli/web3 local-blockchain toolchain. No import of tweetnacl in the project's own code; the toolchain ships it. Shor-vulnerable signature scheme → ML-DSA-65 when the toolchain is upgraded. Same package recorded as LIB-0469707e.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: elliptic@6.3.3 is a transitive dependency (via ethereumjs-util@6.1.0); its ECDH capability is available in the shipped library. The repo's own code reaches elliptic for secp256k1 ECDSA signing, not ECDH — presence in the shipped build is what this object records.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: tweetnacl@0.14.5 declared transitively; its X25519 key agreement is available in the shipped library. No X25519 call site in this repo's own code.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Keccak-256 — Ethereum's pre-standard SHA-3/Keccak-256 variant — used throughout the test and deployment scripts (web3.utils.keccak256, ethereumjs-util keccak256 with EIP-191 "Ethereum Signed Message" prefix) to build message hashes for signature tests, compute CREATE2 payloads, derive action IDs and verify deployed runtime-code hashes.
